title: Intrinsic Information-Theoretic Analysis of ReLU Nets
claim: A network's layered geometric partition of input space reduces to a discrete combinatorial code of per-layer activation patterns.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, geometry panels then neuron-graph with highlighted region
description: Three side-by-side panels. (a) 'After layer 1' shows a 2-D input square with blue (class 0) and red (class 1) scattered points in two interleaved crescent shapes. Black lines cut the square into convex regions, and one region ω is filled yellow and labeled. (b) 'After layer 2' shows the same scatter with many more black lines, so the partition is a finer refinement. The yellow region ω is now smaller, because the new lines split it. (c) 'Region ω identified by π_ω' is a small network diagram with Input (x1, x2), Layer 1 and Layer 2 neurons. Each neuron is marked 0 or 1, with active neurons in green and inactive ones in light gray. Green edges are highlighted between the active neurons. Yellow boxes underneath give the activation patterns π^(1) = (1,0,1,0) and π^(2) = (0,1,0,0). The eye goes first to the yellow region on the left.
caption: From geometry to combinatorics in a ReLU network. (b) Composing the second layer refines the partition: each new hyperplane subdivides regions of (a), so the partition through layer 2 is the common refinement of the per-layer partitions and ω itself is split. abstract: Mutual information (MI) is fundamental to representation-learning analysis in deep networks, but in high dimensions MI estimators depend on hyperparameters whose bias often dominates the signal. We show that continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) networks, including ReLU networks, admit an intrinsic information-theoretic analysis that avoids this pitfall: their inherent partition of the input space into convex linear regions assigns to every input a discrete region label $Î $ alongside the continuous representation $T$ and label $Y$. We introduce a decomposition of the mutual information $I(Y;T)$ into interpretable geometric terms. We show that the dominant term, the *routing information* $I(Y; Î )$, admits an estimable plug-in estimator, that in the well-sampled regime, approximates a population lower bound on the joint information $I(Y; Î , T)$. When the partition saturates, a functional-equivalence quotient collapses regions implementing the same linear operator and restores informativeness; this extension has a single bounded, dimensionless parameter, which is reported through the quotient's compression ratio. The routing estimator agrees strongly with three established MI baselines applied to the same networks and data. The functional quotient recovers informative estimates in the regime bordering the well-sampled and under-sampled regime. We provide a framework for analysing the internal information geometry of CPWL networks, grounded in their inherent piecewise-linear structure rather than in external discretisation.
